q: Were the council to approve the plan, construction ___ next year.
explain: Were + subject + to-infinitive = formal hypothetical → would.

q: Little ___ that the castle had been watching them.
explain: Negative adverbial at the start → inversion: Little did they know.

q: Only after the gates had closed ___ their mistake.
explain: Only after… + inversion in the main clause.

q: It's essential that every member ___ present.
explain: Formal subjunctive after 'essential that': be.

q: ___ the heavy rain, the ceremony went ahead.
explain: Despite + noun; Although + clause; In spite OF.

q: The proposal, ___ merits are obvious, was rejected.
explain: whose + noun = possession.

q: She'd sooner resign than ___ the truth.
explain: would sooner X than Y — both bare infinitives.

q: Not only ___ the treaty, but he also broke it.
explain: Not only + inversion.

q: Hardly had the debate started ___ the lights went out.
explain: Hardly… when; No sooner… than.

q: Should you need assistance, ___ hesitate to ask.
explain: Should you… = If you…; an imperative follows.

q: The minister is said ___ the decision before the vote.
explain: is said + perfect infinitive for an earlier action.

q: What I find most frustrating ___ the lack of transparency.
explain: A what-clause subject takes a singular verb.

q: Rarely ___ such eloquence in the council chamber.
explain: Rarely at the start → inversion.

q: It was the knight's courage, rather than his skill, ___ won the day.
explain: Cleft sentence: It was X that…

q: Had it not been for her intervention, the talks ___.
explain: Had it not been for = If it hadn't been for → would have + p.p.

q: So convincing ___ that the council changed its mind.
explain: So + adjective at the start → inversion with 'be'.

q: Not until much later ___ the full extent of the damage.
explain: Inversion after 'Not until…'.

q: ___ as it may seem, the plan actually worked.
explain: Adjective + as + subject + may seem = although it may seem strange.

q: The council recommended that the bridge ___ closed immediately.
explain: Subjunctive after 'recommend that': base form.

q: What the kingdom needs ___ fewer promises and more action.
explain: A 'what' cleft takes a singular verb.

q: ___ the evidence, the jury had no choice but to acquit.
explain: 'Given' (= considering) introduces a reason.

q: On no account ___ the gates be left open after dark.
explain: Negative inversion: On no account + should + subject.

q: She is thought ___ in secret for years before the treaty was signed.
explain: Passive reporting + perfect continuous infinitive for a long earlier action.

q: ___ the proposal been better presented, it might have passed.
explain: Inverted third conditional.

q: Much as I respect his experience, I ___ with his conclusions.
explain: 'Much as' = although; the clause contrasts respect with disagreement.

q: The more evidence emerged, ___ the minister's position became.
explain: The + comparative…, the + comparative.

q: It's high time the council ___ responsibility.
explain: It's high time + past simple.

q: Only when the treaty was signed ___ relax.
explain: Inversion after 'Only when…'.

q: Were the plan ___, thousands would lose their homes.
explain: Were + subject + to-infinitive (formal conditional).

q: Not a word of complaint ___ from her during the whole ordeal.
explain: Inversion after a fronted negative object.
